title: Lags and growth
summary: Compare each period with the one before: shift, diff, pct_change, month over month and year over year.

steps.title: Looking back with shift
body: Most questions about a time series are comparisons: *did we sell more than last month?* `shift` moves the values
down by n rows so each row lines up with an earlier one:
s.shift(1)            # last period's value, on this row
s - s.shift(1)        # change since last period
s.diff()              # the same thing, built in
The first row has no predecessor, so it becomes NaN. A lag of 1 compares with the previous row; it only means
"previous month" if each row *is* a month, so resample first.

steps.explain: `shift(-1)` pulls the next value up: useful for "what happened next", but it leaks the future if you use it as a feature.

steps.title: Growth rates
body: A change of 20 means a lot for 100 and little for 10,000. Growth is relative:
s.pct_change(12)          # monthly data: vs the same month last year
**Month over month** (MoM) shows momentum, but seasonal businesses swing every December. **Year over year** (YoY)
compares December with last December, so the season cancels out.

steps.prompt: A toy shop's December sales are 40% higher than November's. Which comparison tells you whether the business actually grew?
options: December this year vs December last year
December vs the average of all months
steps.explain: Toy shops boom every December. Only year-over-year compares like with like.

steps.title: Change columns
prompt: Write `add_changes(df)`. `df` is indexed by month and has a `sales` column. Return a **copy** with three new columns:
- `prev`: last month's sales,
- `change`: sales minus `prev`,
- `pct`: the percentage change, rounded to 1 decimal (`25.0` means +25%).
The first month has NaN in all three.
```python
df = pd.DataFrame({"sales": [200.0, 250.0, 225.0, 300.0]}, index=pd.date_range("2024-01-31", periods=4, freq="ME"))
out = add_changes(df)
out["change"].tolist()   # [nan, 50.0, -25.0, 75.0]

steps.title: Year over year
prompt: `monthly` is a Series of 24 monthly totals indexed by month end (2023-01 to 2024-12). Write two functions:
- `yoy(monthly)`: a dict from month (`"2024-01"`) to its growth versus the same month a year earlier, in percent rounded to 1
decimal, for the 12 months of the second year only.
- `best_month(monthly)`: the `"YYYY-MM"` of the month with the highest year-over-year growth.
solution: return {d.strftime("%Y-%m"): float(v) for d, v in growth.items()}
hints: `monthly.pct_change(12)` compares each month with 12 rows earlier.
Drop the NaN first year with `.dropna()`.
`idxmax()` gives the label of the largest growth.
